outcome: Keep the format_not_applied rewrite consistent with the output contract: when the contract the export is held to declares a type for a column that the rewrite's try_cast derive would change to one the contract refuses, the advice names the contract and the declared type and proposes no rewrite, instead of a rewrite whose export fails with CONTRACT_MISMATCH
criteria: With a current output contract that declares a text column of ISO dates as string, an export whose format_spec gives that column a date_format still succeeds and reports format_not_applied; its advice names the contract id, the column, the declared type and the type the try_cast derive would give it, says the contract would refuse the derived dataset's export, points at declare_output with a reason as the way to amend the contract, and carries no rewrite

With no contract, or with a contract that declares that column without a type, the rewrite is still offered and succeeds when every call is sent back as-is; whether the contract accepts the derived columns is decided by the contract's own verify_columns, so declared spellings (MADR 0013) and type families are judged as export_result judges them

Tests in tests/test_export.py cover the declared-string case and the untyped-contract case, sending back every rewrite offered; README.md says the rewrite is withheld when the contract would refuse it

dispositions.note: advise_unapplied_format in agent_backend/core/recovery/advice.py now receives the contract export_result is held to, together with the dataset's column types. test_a_contract_that_declares_the_text_type_withholds_the_rewrite_and_names_the_declaration declares Dispatched as string. It checks that the export succeeds with format_not_applied, that the advice says output contract oc_1 would refuse that export because it declares Dispatched as string while the derive makes dispatched timestamp, that it points at declare_output with a reason, and that it carries no rewrite.

The decision to withhold is verify_columns run on the schema the derive would produce, so MADR 0013 spellings and type families are judged as export_result judges them. test_a_contract_that_declares_no_type_for_the_column_keeps_the_rewrite sends both rewrite calls back: both succeed, the file carries the declared header Dispatched and the formatted dates, and the existing no-contract test still sends its rewrite back successfully.

Both tests are in tests/test_export.py, and the declared-string test fails on the PR head. README.md, under Exporting an answer, says the rewrite is withheld when the contract would refuse it. The full pytest suite passes, and ruff reports no new findings in the changed files.

note: Amending the contract is left to the agent (MADR 0008), and formatting stays at the export boundary (MADR 0005), so the advice explains and does not rewrite when the contract blocks the cast.
